summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old female with a history of type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease status post kidney and pancreas transplants, mechanical mitral valve replacement, and systolic heart failure was admitted for worsening abdominal pain, volume overload, and low-grade fevers. She had gained 5 pounds despite increasing diuretics and reported severe nocturnal epigastric pain. Evaluation revealed fluid overload with mild pulmonary congestion, managed with IV furosemide and the addition of metolazone. Her abdominal pain was attributed to mesenteric ischemia after consultation with gastroenterology, and her GI regimen was adjusted to avoid interactions with tacrolimus. She remained afebrile in hospital with negative infectious workup. Her INR was elevated at 5.5, prompting warfarin hold and discharge on reduced dose. She improved symptomatically and was discharged home with new prescriptions, including morphine for pain, and instructions to monitor weight and follow up with cardiology and GI specialists.
